text:
Alicia: FYI Nimbus Health is asking for a Dedicated commit quote. They want a 12mo commit, baseline 3x A100s, autoscale to 6 for steady peaks, burst to 12 for short events. Also asking for a 15% concession on list. Need deal desk + engineering signoff.

CJ: Noted. Can we get POC sizing + expected QPS/p95 so eng can confirm baseline? Also please drop the legal/data residency checklist.

Maria: We ran a quick POC last week — customer sees ~120 rps at 512 tokens, p95 ~220ms on batch=8 with 4x A100. For the committed pool, 3A100 baseline is tight during peak. Recommend baseline 4A100 or autoscale window set to 6.

Sam: Agree with Maria. Autoscale policy we usually recommend: scale to 6 when sustained 90s of CPU/GPU queue > 70%, burst to 12 for max 10 minutes per hour. Cold start to new nodes ~30–45s. If they need <5s tail latency at peak we should bump baseline.

Hannah: Also flag: fallback policy for Dedicated to Hosted is turned on by default, but for enterprise we can lock it off. That affects availability during saturation — if they want strict isolation we need dedicated-only SLA and corresponding price uplift.

Omar: Rate card snapshot:
```
Dedicated A100 monthly list (per GPU): $8,400
Baseline pool pricing = GPUs_in_pool * per-GPU rate
Autoscale burst premium = +50% on additional burst GPUs when active
Commit discount tiers: 6mo=5%, 12mo=10%, 24mo=18% (standard)
Special concession requested: 15% -> needs approval from VP-Finance
```

Leah: Data residency: Nimbus requires EU data at rest and customer-managed KMS. We can support via Private deployment (VPC) for Dedicated, addendum required. Also will need a security questionnaire (SAQ) and SOC attestation attach.

Alicia: Key ask from sales: show them a worked example monthly invoice for 12mo with 4A100 baseline, autoscale to 6 typical, burst-to-12 occasional, and our proposed 12% discount (we're offering less than they asked to start).

Omar: Quick calc (monthly):
- baseline 4 GPUs * $8,400 = $33,600
- autoscale capacity (2 extra GPUs avg) billed at 1.5x when active -> 2 * $8,400 * 1.5 * utilization_fraction(0.2) ≈ $5,040
- burst (occasional) not charged continuously, accrues as overage at burst premium; estimate $1,200/month
Subtotal = $39,840
12% commit discount -> -$4,780
Estimated monthly = $35,060
Annual = $420,720
(Numbers rough; spreadsheet link updated)

deploy-bot: Spreadsheets updated: https://redwood.co/spreadsheets/nimbus-dedicated-1763608123 (view only) :white_check_mark:

CJ: This looks reasonable. For a 12% concession we need documented business reason: long-term upsell potential + marketplace deal. I'll queue for Deal Desk approval. @Omar please confirm margin impact and escalate to VP-Finance if >10% concession.

Omar: Margin impact ~8% on expected runtime costs; finance ok to approve up to 12% on this deal if we get ARR > $400k and 12mo commit. I'll flag VP-Finance for an explicit sign-off.

Hannah: Ops note: If we disable Hosted fallback for strict isolation we add an SLA penalty window for cross-zone failures. Ops will need a runbook and 1-week lead for capacity reservation.

Leah: I'll prep the addendum and the KMS language. Security questionnaire — ask Nimbus to fill the SAQ 1 and we can attach SOC2 type II.

Alicia: Thanks all. Next steps: (1) Maria/Sam finalize POC perf notes and recommended baseline (2) Omar finalize pricing deck and get VP sign-off for 12% (3) Leah prepare addendum & SAQ request (4) CJ submit to Deal Desk with business justification. Aiming to reply to customer EOD tomorrow.

Maria: I'll post the perf export and POC logs into the sheet by EOD.

Sam: I'll add recommended autoscale policy snippet:
```
autoscale:
  baseline_gpus: 4
  scale_up_threshold: 70% queue
  scale_up_window: 90s
  max_burst: 12
  burst_duration_limit: 10m/hour
```

CJ: Kicking off Deal Desk ticket now. Ticket #DD-2026-0091. Will post approval here when I have it.

Omar: VP-Finance notified (cc'd). If approved I will publish final rate quote and terms.

Alicia: @CJ @Omar please loop me when you have approvals — I have a call with Nimbus Tuesday 09:30 PT. :pray:
